alex.g: Quick question — where do I find TTFT / p95 / p99 for hosted API token flows? Trying to tune the alert that fired this morning. Anyone have dashboard links, PromQL snippets, or runbook pointers? @sasha @priya

sasha: Dashboards are in Grafana — main ones are 'Inference Latency Overview' and 'Tokenflow / Throughput'. Links: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/latency/inference-overview and https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/tokenflow/tokenflow-summary

Here are a couple quick PromQLs I use: 
```
# p95 TTFT by model (from summary/histogram buckets)
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_request_ttft_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model))

# tokens/sec rolling 1m by model
sum(rate(redwood_tokens_emitted_total[1m])) by (model)
```

Notes: TTFT = time-to-first-token (measured server-side after request accepted). If you only have summary metrics (not buckets) use rate(redwood_request_ttft_seconds_sum[5m]) / rate(redwood_request_ttft_seconds_count[5m]) for p50-ish estimates, but buckets + histogram_quantile is better.

priya: For alerting heuristics we've been using: p95 > 1.2s for small models, p95 > 2.5s for larger autoregressives, p99 > 4s as a high-severity. Also alert on sustained drop in tokens/sec: if sum(rate(redwood_tokens_emitted_total[5m])) by (cluster) < 20% of baseline for > 3m it's often a cache/cold-start issue.

Sample alert rule (Prometheus style):
```
- alert: TTFT_P95_High
  expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_request_ttft_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model)) > 1.2
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "High TTFT p95 for {{ $labels.model }}"
    description: "p95 TTFT above 1.2s for 5m. Check model pool, batching and cache hit rates."
```

morgan: Traces + logs: we can jump from the Grafana panels to Tempo traces (link in the panel) — look for service=runtime and span names like `emit_first_token`. Tempo search: https://tempo.redwood.internal/search?service=runtime&span=emit_first_token.

Logs are in Loki, query example: `{job="runtime", model="mistral-7b"} |= "request_id=" | json | request_id="<id>"` — that helps correlate trace->request->logs.

alex.g: This is super helpful — thanks. If I tune the alert thresholds, should I also add a low-severity warning channel first? Last time it paged at 3am.

priya: Yes, recommend two-tier: warning (slack only) at p95 > threshold for 5m, page at p99 > higher threshold or if tokens/sec drops drastically. Also add runbook link in alert annotations: https://wiki.redwood.internal/runbooks/ttft
